title: Fish Rugs: Sizes, Prices and Koi Designs Compared
meta_description: Fish rugs from $21.90 to $123.90 across 11 designs. Compare pond-shaped koi rugs and rectangles by size, price, non-slip backing and personalization.
body_html:
A fish rug from Chillgen costs $21.90 to $123.90. Which one is right depends on three things: the floor space you measure, whether you want a pond-shaped koi rug or a rectangle, and whether you want it personalized.

The sections below take those decisions one at a time, and each ends with a short list to check before you order. One hypothetical example runs through every section so you can see each decision being made.

Contents

  1. What's in the Fishing Rugs collection?
  2. What size fish rug do you need?
  3. Koi pond shaped rug or rectangular rug?
  4. Which koi fish rug design suits your room?
  5. Will a fish rug stay put, and can it go outdoors?
  6. Is a personalized koi rug worth it?

What's in the Fishing Rugs collection?

The collection has 11 products, priced from $21.90 to $123.90. The six designs featured on this page are all koi pond scenes, and most are cut to an irregular pond outline instead of a straight-edged rectangle.

Every product page uses one of two size menus. It helps to know which one you're looking at:

  • Square sizes: 18"x18", 24"x24", 36"x36", 48"x48", 60"x60" and 72"x72". Some pages label these M (24"x24"), L (36"x36"), XL (48"x48"), 2XL (60"x60") and 3XL (72"x72").
  • Inch sizes, including rectangles: 16 x 16, 16 x 24, 20 x 32 and 24 x 36 inches.

The two menus overlap at the small end and split at the large end. The square menu goes up to 72"x72", while the largest size on the inch menu is 24 x 36 inches. If you need a rug bigger than 24 x 36, look for a product that uses the square menu.

To see all 11 side by side before you narrow it down, browse every fish rug in one place.

How to apply it: before you look at designs, decide whether you need a square or a long rectangle. That one choice tells you which size menu to look for, and so which products to open.

What to check

  • Which size menu the product page shows
  • Whether the size you want is on that menu
  • The starting price for that exact size, not the "from" price on the collection card

What size fish rug do you need?

Measure the floor before you look at prices. Note the width and depth of the space with a tape measure. Then take off any room you want to keep clear for a door swing, chair legs or a cabinet door. Compare what's left with the table below.

The square menu also offers 60"x60" (2XL) and 72"x72" (3XL). The facts we hold don't give a starting price for either, so select the size on the product page to see what it costs.

Worked example (hypothetical). Say you have a spot inside a back door that's wider than 36 inches but less than 36 inches deep, and more than 24 inches deep. A 36"x36" rug is out because it's too deep. Two sizes fit:

  • 24"x24", from $31.90: fits both ways, with spare floor on every side.
  • 24 x 36 in, from $37.89: fits if the 36-inch side runs across the width of the doorway.

What to check

  • Width and depth of the space, minus any clearance you need
  • That the rug's longer side runs the way you want
  • The price for your exact size on the product page

Koi pond shaped rug or rectangular rug?

A shaped koi rug follows an irregular pond outline, so it looks like a small pond on the floor rather than a mat. A rectangle covers the whole marked area edge to edge.

The product pages don't say how the listed size applies to a shaped rug. In particular, they don't say whether the size is the outer box the pond outline fits inside. Look closely at the product photos, or ask the shop before ordering if that matters for your space. If the listed size is the outer box, a shaped rug covers less floor than a rectangle with the same numbers.

How to apply it: mark the listed size on the floor with masking tape. A shaped rug sits inside that outline and leaves some floor showing at the edges. If you want something underfoot every time someone steps in, a rectangle covers more. If the rug is mostly there to be looked at, the pond outline does that better.

Worked example, continued. For the back-door spot, the rectangle (24 x 36 in, from $37.89) covers more of the floor. The shaped koi rug (24"x24", from $31.90) costs less and leaves floor showing around it. Say this household wants the koi scene to be the first thing people see when they come in. They pick the shaped 24"x24".

What to check

  • How the listed size applies to the shape (ask if the page doesn't say)
  • A masking-tape outline at the listed size on your floor
  • Whether you want full coverage or a decorative outline

Which koi fish rug design suits your room?

These six koi designs are in the collection. Five start at $24.90 and one at $31.90. Each line links to that rug's page:

  • Pond scene with a Japanese garden floor and an irregular outline, from $24.90: see the garden-floor koi pond
  • Blue water with raked sand garden lines, from $24.90: see the blue zen pond with sand lines
  • Stepping stones with a mossy garden texture, from $24.90: see the mossy stepping-stone pond
  • Lily pad border on dark teal, from $24.90: see the dark teal lily pad design
  • Winding pond with lily pads in a softer scene, from $24.90: see the soft winding-pond scene
  • Japanese koi pond with a 3D-style design, from $31.90: see the 3D-style koi pond rug

How to apply it: hold a phone photo of your floor and walls next to each design's main image. Blue and teal scenes look different against warm wood than against grey tile. The moss and stone design brings green into the room. The softer winding-pond scene keeps contrast low.

Worked example, continued. The five $24.90 designs start at 18"x18", but the back-door spot needs 24"x24". The household opens the blue sand-line design and checks that 24"x24" is on its size menu before going further.

What to check

  • The colors in the main image next to a photo of your floor
  • That your size is on that design's menu
  • The price shown once your size is selected

Will a fish rug stay put, and can it go outdoors?

Here is what the product pages say about construction, and how many of the 11 pages say it:

  • Anti-slip pads: "Includes anti-slip pads to keep it securely in place", on 11 of 11 pages
  • Edges: "Reinforced serged edges enhance durability", on 6 of 11 pages
  • Pile: "Made with low pile polypropylene for easy cleaning", on 5 of 11 pages
  • Where it's used: "works beautifully across multiple indoor rooms", on 5 of 11 pages

Anti-slip pads are the only feature every page lists. Serged edges and low-pile polypropylene appear on only some pages, so check the page of the rug you want instead of assuming.

If you were searching for an outdoor fish rug, the product pages don't describe any of these rugs for patios, porches or other outdoor use. The pages that mention placement talk about indoor rooms only, so treat these as indoor rugs unless a product page says otherwise. On cleaning, the pages say only "easy cleaning" for the low-pile models and give no washing instructions, so ask the shop before you wash one.

Worked example, continued. At a back door, grip and edges matter more than they would in a bedroom. The household checks the blue sand-line page for the serged-edge line. If it isn't there, they compare the other koi designs that list it.

What to check

  • That the product page mentions anti-slip pads (all 11 do)
  • Whether this rug's page lists serged edges
  • Whether it lists low-pile polypropylene, if easy cleaning matters to you
  • Indoor placement only, unless the page says otherwise

Is a personalized koi rug worth it?

Seven of the 11 product pages say the rug "supports customization with personalized options." The other four don't mention it, so not every design can be personalized.

The pages don't spell out what you can change, whether you see a preview before the rug is made, or how long a personalized order takes. Check the options shown on the product page itself, and ask the shop about previews and timing if you have a date to meet.

How to apply it: decide what you'd add before you shop, because that tells you which of the seven pages to look at. A family name or a short line fits the corner of a 24"x24" rug better than a long phrase. On a shaped rug, look at where text can go so it doesn't land on a lily pad or a fish.

Worked example, finished. The household's final pick is a 24"x24" koi pond rug from $31.90, in a design whose page lists anti-slip pads, serged edges and personalization, with their family name added. If the blue sand-line design doesn't list both edges and personalization, they move to the next koi design that does.

What to check

  • That the product page says it supports personalized options
  • Which options appear on that design's page
  • Where text will sit on the pond outline
  • The final price with your size selected

Once you have your measurements and know whether you want a shape or a rectangle, compare all 11 fishing rugs by size and price and open the two or three that match.
